(Lauderdale Lakes, Florida) | college = [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] (2006–2010) | draft_year = 2010 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 57 | draft_team = [[Indiana Pacers]] | career_start = 2010 | career_end = 2019 | career_number = 33 | career_position = [[Power forward]] | years1 = [[2010–11 NBA Development League season|2010–2011]] | team1 = [[Tulsa 66ers]] | years2 = {{nbay|2011|full=y}} | team2 = [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] | years3 = [[2011–12 NBA Development League season|2012]] | team3 = →Tulsa 66ers | years4 = 2012 | team4 = [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Mets de Guaynabo]] | years5 = 2012–2014 | team5 = [[Chorale Roanne Basket|Chorale Roanne]] | years6 = 2014–2015 | team6 = [[SLUC Nancy Basket|SLUC Nancy]] | years7 = 2015–2016 | team7 = [[Niigata Albirex BB]] | years8 = 2016–2017 | team8 = [[Shimane Susanoo Magic]] | years9 = {{nblcy|2017|end}} | team9 = [[St. John's Edge]] | years10 = 2018–2019 | team10 = [[Kanazawa Samuraiz]] | highlights = }} '''Ryan Rupert Reid''' (October 30, 1986 – July 9, 2025) was an American professional [[basketball]] player. Reid played [[college basketball]] with the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]]. After four years in college, he was drafted by the [[Indiana Pacers]] with the 57th pick in the [[2010 NBA draft]]. After the draft, his draft rights were immediately traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. However, the Thunder did not sign him to a contract and Reid went on to play for the [[Tulsa 66ers]], the [[NBA Development League]] (NBA D-League) affiliate of the Thunder. He played for the 66ers for one season before he was signed by the Thunder for the [[2011–12 NBA season|2011–12 season]]. ==Early life== Ryan Reid was born to Jasmine and Kenneth Mullings. He was born and grew up in [[Lauderdale Lakes, Florida]]. He attended and played for [[Boyd H. Anderson High School|Boyd Anderson High School]] in his hometown. During his last three years with Boyd Anderson, he averaged 18 points, 12 rebounds and 3 blocked shots. After graduating in 2005, he attended [[Florida State University]]. He reportedly chose Florida State over [[University of Florida|Florida]], [[University of Miami|Miami]], [[University of Georgia|Georgia]], [[University of Houston|Houston]] and [[University of Pittsburgh|Pittsburgh]]. He also played basketball in the [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) with the Tallahassee Wildcats.{{cite web|url=http://www.seminoles.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/reid_ryan01.html|title=Florida State Seminoles Player Bio: Ryan Reid|work=Seminoles.com|publisher=CBS Interactive|access-date=December 9, 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130202051747/http://www.seminoles.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/reid_ryan01.html|archive-date=February 2, 2013}} ==College career== Reid played under coach [[Leonard Hamilton]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]], who played in the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] in the [[National Collegiate Athletic Association]] (NCAA) [[NCAA Division I|Division I]]. As a [[freshman]], he played in all 35 games off the bench, averaging 2.9 points on 56.2 percent shooting and 3.2 rebounds in 16.1 minutes per game. In his sophomore season, he started 21 games and played a total of 25 games for the Seminoles. He improved his performance and averaged 5.6 points on 53.1 percent shooting and 5.0 rebounds in 24.1 minutes per game. He helped the Seminoles to the [[National Invitation Tournament]] (NIT) tournament in both years.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/tulsa/66ers_add_ryan_reid__roster_2010_11_26.html|title=66ers Add Ryan Reid to Roster|date=November 26, 2010|work=NBA.com/DLeague|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=December 9, 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101201210555/http://www.nba.com/dleague/tulsa/66ers_add_ryan_reid__roster_2010_11_26.html|archive-date=December 1, 2010}} Reid played 35 games in his junior year, averaging 4.9 points on 44.0 percent shooting and 3.7 rebounds in 19.1 minutes per game. In his final year at college, Reid was named as the team captain.{{cite web |last=Silva |first=Chris |date=June 29, 2010 |title=Reid Made Mark On Defensive End At Florida State |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/reidbio_100629.html |access-date=July 11, 2025 |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc}} He played in 31 games and averaged 6.8 points on 49.1 percent shooting and 4.0 rebounds in 22.7 minutes per game.{{cite web |title=Ryan Reid College Stats |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/stats/_/id/4286/type/mens-college-basketball |access-date=July 11, 2025 |work=ESPN.com |publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures}} He helped the Seminoles to the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA championships]] in his junior and senior seasons. Despite his low scoring and rebounding numbers, his biggest contribution for the Seminoles came at the defensive end. He became one of the best defenders in the college and successfully defended top opposing players.{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2010/03/05/unsung-ryan-reid-does-all-the-little-things-and-does-them-well-for-the-florida-state-seminoles/|title=Unsung Ryan Reid does all the little things — and does them well — for the Florida State Seminoles|first=Andrew|last=Carter|date=March 5, 2010|work=Orlando Sentinel|publisher=Tribune Company|access-date=December 9, 2010}} He became one of only three players in the Seminoles history to reach the postseason in all four years. Reid, who helped the Seminoles to 88 wins, also had more wins than any other player in school history. He finished his college career with 126 games with 5.0 points per game and 3.7 rebounds per game average. He graduated with a bachelor's degree in [[social science]] on May 1, 2010, and became the first person in his family to earn a college degree.{{cite web |date=May 3, 2010 |title=Ryan Reid -- Graduate |url=http://www.seminoles.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/050310aab.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120910151613/http://www.seminoles.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/050310aab.html |archive-date=September 10, 2012 |access-date=December 9, 2010 |work=Seminoles.com |publisher=CBS Interactive}} ==Professional career== Reid was [[Eligibility for the NBA draft|automatically eligible]] for the [[2010 NBA draft]] after finishing his four-year college eligibility. The [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] were the only NBA team that sought to see him play or practice before the draft.{{cite web|url=https://www.orlandosentinel.com/2010/07/16/florida-states-ryan-reid-goes-on-improbable-journey-from-role-player-to-nba-draft-pick/|title=Florida State's Ryan Reid goes on improbable journey from role player to NBA Draft pick|first=Andrew|last=Carter|date=July 16, 2010|work=Orlando Sentinel|publisher=Tribune Company|access-date=December 9, 2010}} He was eventually drafted by the [[Indiana Pacers]] with the 57th pick in the draft and his rights were immediately traded to the Thunder in exchange for the rights to [[Magnum Rolle]], the 51st pick.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/team_release2_2010_06_25.html|title=Thunder Acquires Pleiss, Williams, Reid and Future First Round Pick in 2010 NBA Draft|date=June 24, 2010|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=June 25, 2010}} His selection was considered a surprise in the draft because some analysts did not even consider him as a top-100 prospect for the draft.{{cite web |last=Biderman |first=David |date=July 14, 2010 |title=Meet the Nba's Non-LeBron |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052748704518904575365154204015926 |access-date=July 11, 2025 |work=The Wall Street Journal |publisher=Dow Jones & Company, Inc}} Nevertheless, the Thunder was already impressed with Reid's defensive abilities and work ethic and decided to take a chance on him. He played for the Thunder in the [[2010 NBA Summer League|2010 Orlando Summer League]]. He played in four games, averaging 8.3 points and 3.8 rebounds in 16.0 minutes per game.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/summerleague2010/players/ryan_reid/|title=2010 NBA Summer League Statistics – Ryan Reid|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=December 9, 2010}} However, he did not receive a contract offer or an invitation to the Thunder's training camp for the [[2010–11 NBA season|2010–11 season]].{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/nba/2010-09-28-1282959531_x.htm|title=Thunder open training camp|date=September 28, 2010|work=USA Today|publisher=Gannett Co, Inc|access-date=December 9, 2010}} On November 26, 2010, he was acquired by the [[Tulsa 66ers]], the D-League affiliate of the Thunder. His rights in the NBA were still held by the Thunder. Hence, the Thunder was the only team allowed to call up Reid to the NBA during the [[2010–11 NBA Development League season|2010–11 season]]. He averaged 8.5 points on 50.3 percent shooting and 5.8 rebounds per game in 48 games with the 66ers.{{cn|date=July 2025}} He returned to the 66ers for the [[2011–12 NBA Development League season|2011–12 season]]. After playing 8 games and averaging 11.8 points and 8.9 rebounds per game, he was called up to the Thunder training camp roster on December 13, 2011.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_reid_111213.html|title=Thunder Adds Reid to Training Camp Roster|date=December 13, 2011|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=January 19, 2012}} On January 16, 2012, Reid returned to the 66ers on assignment from the Thunder.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/release_reid_120116.html|title=Ryan Reid Assigned to Tulsa 66ers|date=January 16, 2012|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=January 19, 2012}} He was recalled on February 6, 2012.{{Cite web |date=2012-02-06 |title=Thunder recall Reid from D-League |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/nba/thunder-recall-reid-from-d-league |access-date=2025-07-11 |website=foxsports.com |language=en-US}} On March 16, 2012, Reid was reassigned to the 66ers.{{cite web|url=http://www.newson6.com/story/17178966/oklahoma-city-assigns-reid-to-d-league-team |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120905063504/http://www.newson6.com/story/17178966/oklahoma-city-assigns-reid-to-d-league-team |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 5, 2012 |title=Oklahoma City assigns Reid to D-League team |date=January 16, 2012 |work=The Associated Press |access-date=January 25, 2012 }} He was recalled and then waived on March 21, 2012.{{cite web |date=March 21, 2012 |title=Thunder Signs Derek Fisher |url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/fisher_release_120321.html |access-date=July 11, 2025 |work=NBA.com |publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc}} He then returned to the 66ers on March 23, 2012. On November 17, 2014, he signed with [[SLUC Nancy Basket|SLUC Nancy]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/141450/sluc-nancy-lands-ryan-reid.html SLUC Nancy lands Ryan Reid] On February 14, 2018, he signed with the [[St. John's Edge]] of [[NBL Canada]].{{cite web|title=Edge Sign Power Forward, Ryan Reid|date=14 February 2018 |url=http://sjedge.ca/RyanReid|publisher=St. John's Edge|access-date=14 February 2018}} == Death == Ryan Reid died following a medical emergency on July 9, 2025, at the age of 38.{{cite web |last1=Schoffel |first1=Ira |date=July 10, 2025
